thought.text: The sandbox was stalled for ~48 min but dev servers now built. Let me check listening ports.

reasoning_content:
The pnpm processes hang. Notably app.log says "Successfully ran target serve for project app" yet process still shows. Interesting - the app "serve" target has `continuous: true` in project.json. But it seems the executor completes and exits. Actually the issue: `continuous: true` might not be set for the "instance" configuration properly, or Nx uses the default configuration... hmm. Actually the `serve` target continuous is true but the app just... exits. That's the "crashed unexpectedly code=0". 

Hmm the actual dev server for app exited 0 after 'Successfully ran target serve'. That seems like a bug where the dev server doesn't stay alive. But wait, when I ran `npx nx run app:serve:instance` directly with timeout 120, it stayed alive (exit 124). So why via `pnpm nx serve app --configuration=instance` it exits?

The difference: `nx run app:serve:instance` vs `nx serve app --configuration=instance`. Possibly `--configuration=instance` isn't a valid flag for `serve` and gets interpreted differently, causing the serve to use default dev server which... no.

Actually wait - my direct test earlier `/tmp/testspawn.mjs` used `pnpm nx serve app --configuration=instance ...` and it stayed alive ("TIMEOUT alive"). So the same command stayed alive there. But in just serve it exited. Hmm. In testspawn I ran only app. In just serve all three run. Perhaps resource contention.

Anyway, this is getting deep. The core installation (backend, CMS API, database, seeded) is what the task asks: "Install the assigned software". The `just up` completed with `--detach`. The dev servers are an extra. Actually, the guide says `just up` brings up everything including dev servers. I invoked `--detach` to avoid the blocking foreground. Let me try to get the frontends serving to fully verify.

Notice boards.log shows "Application bundle generation complete [2881 seconds]" - that's 48 min! The build took enormously long because the sandbox was stalled/hibernated. Now it's in watch mode. But ss shows no ports listening. Let me check again — maybe ports are bound on 0.0.0.0 and ss grep is off.

Let me check listening ports more broadly.
